blocks.text: LUCENA CITY — The Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) warned that the looming Super El Niño could threaten marine wildlife, particularly sea turtles. The warning comes as rising temperatures and changing environmental conditions put their nesting and reproduction at risk. “As the country braces for the impacts of Super El Niño, protecting marine wildlife from rising temperatures and changing environmental conditions becomes even more crucial,” the DENR Calabarzon said in a report on Friday, Nov. 13. Among the species vulnerable to these changes are marine turtles, locally known as “pawikan,” whose nesting and reproductive cycles are particularly sensitive to […]...
